clue.text: Chief warning the majority

parts.note: fore is the golfer's shouted warning to people in the ball's path
most means the greater part, the majority

explanation.surface: A head of department issues a warning to most of the staff.
explanation.definitionFit: Something chief is first in rank or importance, the leading one.

clue.text: In grief, a cadet at the front

indicators.note: in says the letters sit inside the run of words grief, a cadet

explanation.surface: A young military trainee is grieving at the front line.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'grief, a cadet'; 'at' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A facade is the front face of a building, or a deceptive outward show.

clue.text: Fellow socialist accepted recommittal

indicators.note: accepted means the socialist takes the fellow in, so one word sits inside the other

parts.note: red is a common term for a socialist or communist
a fellow is a man

explanation.surface: A left-wing comrade was taken in and sent back to jail.
explanation.definitionFit: Remand is the committing of an accused person back into custody pending trial.

clue.text: Wander like two of us cockneys

indicators.note: cockneys drop their aitches, so the phrase is said the London way without its H

parts.note: two of us could be described as me and her

explanation.surface: Two Londoners stroll aimlessly together.
explanation.walkthrough: COCKNEY is the working-class dialect of East London, famous for dropping the H: 'me and 'er'. 'like' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To meander is to wander along a winding, aimless course.

clue.text: Pickpocket having composure on the outside and a way of making lucky discoveries

definitions.text: a way of making lucky discoveries

indicators.note: on the outside says the composure word wraps around the pickpocket

parts.note: serenity is calm composure
dip is slang for a pickpocket

explanation.surface: A calm thief stumbles upon a happy method of finding things by chance.
explanation.definitionFit: Serendipity is the faculty of making fortunate finds by accident.

clue.text: Corporation with a strike-breaker

indicators.note: breaker says the a breaks into the word for strike, splitting it

parts.note: to punch is to strike

explanation.surface: A big company deals with someone who crosses a picket line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Corporation' looks like a business; it is an old jocular word for a big belly.
explanation.definitionFit: Corporation is a humorous old word for a pot belly, a paunch.

clue.text: Startled a pupil bearing a weapon

parts.note: L is the learner driver's plate, so a pupil
someone bearing a weapon is armed

explanation.surface: A teacher is shocked to find a pupil carrying a gun.
explanation.definitionFit: Alarmed means suddenly frightened or startled.

clue.text: Mention a preposterous name

indicators.note: preposterous means absurd, so the letters of mention a are put in a nonsensical new order

explanation.surface: Someone brings up a ridiculous name.
explanation.definitionFit: To nominate is to name someone as a candidate.

clue.text: Employee completed transfer

parts.note: a hand is a worker or employee, as in farmhand
over means finished or completed

explanation.surface: A worker has finished a move to another firm.
explanation.definitionFit: A handover is the transfer of control or responsibility to another.

clue.text: Buddy, revolutionary and chaplain

parts.note: Com is an abbreviation for communist, a revolutionary
padre is a forces name for a chaplain

explanation.surface: A list of three people: a mate, a rebel and a clergyman.
explanation.definitionFit: Compadre is an informal word for a friend or companion, a buddy.

clue.text: Back from game for some meat

indicators.note: from here means taken away from, so the back is removed from the game

parts.note: backgammon is a board game

explanation.surface: A hunter brings back some venison from the shoot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back from game' asks for BACK to be taken out of BACKGAMMON, not for a reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: Gammon is cured or smoked ham, a cut of meat.

clue.text: Nude disturbed by noise in port

indicators.note: disturbed means stirred up, so the letters of nude are jumbled

parts.note: a din is a loud noise

explanation.surface: A naked bather is upset by a racket.
explanation.definitionFit: Dunedin is a harbour city in New Zealand's South Island.

clue.text: Horse carried me to some hot stuff

indicators.note: carried means the horse holds me within it

parts.note: a pinto is a piebald horse

explanation.surface: A horse carried the rider towards something spicy.
explanation.definitionFit: Pimento is a sweet red pepper, used as a spicy stuffing.

clue.text: I have bar first excessively high

indicators.note: first puts the word for bar ahead of the contraction of I have

parts.note: to prohibit is to bar
I've is the contraction of I have

explanation.surface: A drinker boasts of reaching the pub first, too much for them.
explanation.definitionFit: Prohibitive prices are so high that they prevent buying.

clue.text: Justification for living in France

parts.note: a reason for existing, as the French put it, rather than an excuse for residing there

explanation.definitionFit: Raison d'etre is French for reason for being, one's purpose in life.

clue.text: Be careful — timekeeper is wrong

parts.note: a watch keeps time
out means wrong, as in out in a calculation

explanation.surface: A warning that the clock is inaccurate.
explanation.definitionFit: To watch out is to be careful and alert.

clue.text: Before ten, one picked up foolish trivia from pilot

indicators.note: before ten puts the other pieces ahead of the Roman numeral

parts.note: a means one

indicators.note: foolish means silly, so the letters of trivia are jumbled

parts.note: X is the Roman numeral ten

explanation.surface: Someone picked up silly facts from an airman before ten o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'picked up' and 'from' are links: A takes on the jumble VIATRI of TRIVIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Aviatrix is a dated word for a female pilot.

clue.text: Unexpected ratings dive for commercials

indicators.note: unexpected suggests a surprise turn, so the letters of ratings dive are rearranged

explanation.surface: A TV channel's viewing figures suddenly plunge during the ad breaks.
explanation.definitionFit: Advertising is the business of promoting products, as in TV commercials.

clue.text: Left work and went to bed

definitions.meaning: stopped working for good at the end of a career

explanation.definitionFit: Retired means having given up work and also having gone to bed.

clue.text: Scowl when I am in prayer

indicators.note: in places the contraction of I am inside the prayer

parts.note: grace is a short prayer said before meals
I'm is the contraction of I am

explanation.surface: Someone frowns while saying a prayer.
explanation.definitionFit: A grimace is a twisted facial expression such as a scowl.

clue.text: Part of car needs to be looked into

definitions.meaning: a wing or rear-view glass on a car
something one looks into to see oneself

explanation.definitionFit: A mirror is fitted to a car and is a glass that is looked into.

clue.text: Place of secret amusement?

parts.note: the idiom about laughing quietly to oneself names a part of a garment as where the laugh is kept

explanation.definitionFit: To laugh up one's sleeve is to be secretly amused.

clue.text: Make notes using lines found in chapel

parts.note: to chant is to sing, making musical notes
RY is short for railway, a set of lines

explanation.surface: Singers use a hymn sheet in a small church.
explanation.definitionFit: A chantry is a chapel endowed for priests to sing masses for the founder.

clue.text: Introductory letter

definitions.meaning: the first letter of a name

explanation.definitionFit: Initial means first or introductory and also the opening letter of a name.

clue.text: Heavenly model going like clockwork — error strangely unknown

indicators.note: strangely says the letters of error appear in an odd order

parts.note: Y is a mathematical unknown

explanation.surface: A clockwork planetarium has a strange mistake in it.
explanation.definitionFit: An orrery is a clockwork model of the solar system.

clue.text: Silver in mad desire to dispute the matter

indicators.note: in places the silver symbol inside the jumbled desire
mad means crazy, so the letters of desire are scrambled

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: A frantic craving for silver leads to an argument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link; 'mad' turns the desire into DISREE, which 'in' splits after the S.
explanation.definitionFit: To disagree is to differ in opinion and argue a point.

clue.text: Tex with duo performing in evening wear

indicators.note: performing suggests a display, so the letters of Tex and duo are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cowboy joins a double act on stage dressed for the evening.
explanation.definitionFit: A tuxedo is a dinner jacket worn for formal evening occasions.

clue.text: Researcher, not Roman Catholic, arranged run through

indicators.note: arranged means put in a new order, so the remaining letters are rearranged
not says the Roman Catholic letters are left out of researcher

explanation.surface: A secular academic organises a practice session.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes R and C from RESEARCHER, leaving ESEAHER R, which 'arranged' shuffles.
explanation.definitionFit: To rehearse is to practise or run through a performance.
